fact.text: Aerosmith reportedly made more money from the video game Guitar Hero: Aerosmith than from any one of their own albums.

heads_up: Šią savaitę lietų keis šlapdriba, keliuose galimas plikledis.
Nuo pirmadienio dalyje mokyklų ir darželių streikuoja pedagogai.

lithuania.headline: Prasideda neterminuotas mokytojų streikas
lithuania.summary: LŠDPS nuo pirmadienio pradeda neterminuotą streiką, prie kurio, profsąjungos duomenimis, jungiasi 222 švietimo įstaigos, tarp jų ir darželiai. Vyriausybė kitąmet siūlo mokytojų algas didinti 7,56 proc. (245 mln. eurų), o profsąjunga reikalauja 10 proc.
lithuania.context: Andriaus Navicko vadovaujama LŠDPS neterminuotai streikavo 2018 m., o 2023 m. dalis pedagogų nedirbo nuo rugsėjo pabaigos iki gruodžio vidurio, kol buvo priimtas biudžetas. Pernai profsąjunga vėl grasino streiku, bet ministerija rado papildomų 100 mln. eurų. Pagal nacionalinį švietimo susitarimą pedagogų alga turi siekti 130 proc. šalies vidutinio darbo užmokesčio, dabar ji nesiekia 120 proc.

lithuania.headline: Kontrolierė kritikuoja „valstiečių“ referendumą dėl šeimos
lithuania.summary: „Valstiečiai“ koalicijoje reikalauja patariamojo referendumo, ar šeimos santykiai kyla tik iš vyro ir moters santuokos. Lygių galimybių kontrolierė Birutė Sabatauskaitė sako, kad jo tikslai neaiškūs, o referendumas tik skaldytų visuomenę.
lithuania.context: Šeimos sampratos ginčas Lietuvoje tęsiasi daugiau nei dešimtmetį, ypač dėl partnerystės įteisinimo. Konstitucinis Teismas pripažino, kad pagalbinio apvaisinimo kompensavimas tik sutuoktiniams diskriminuoja, ir Seimas neseniai priėmė platesnį Pagalbinio apvaisinimo įstatymą, kuris leis paslauga naudotis ir vienišoms moterims. Po to „valstiečiai“ pareikalavo referendumo.

lithuania.headline: Lietuvos banko vadovas abejoja mokesčių lengvatomis
lithuania.summary: Lietuvos banko vadovas įvardijo mokesčių lengvatas, kurios, jo vertinimu, nėra reikalingos, ir ragina kelti klausimą dėl jų atsisakymo.
lithuania.context: Vyriausybė, rengdama 2027 m. biudžetą, ieško būdų taupyti, o diskusijos dėl lengvatų vyksta kartu su ginčais dėl atlyginimų didinimo.

world.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin to hold first three-way summit
world.summary: China confirmed that Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin will meet on Thursday in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit that starts Wednesday. Analysts call it symbolic and doubt a 'Yalta 2.0' deal on Ukraine or Taiwan.
world.context: It is the first such meeting of the three leaders. Trump heads to Asia two weeks after his party lost the US midterm elections, hoping to regain momentum abroad. APEC economies make up more than 60% of global GDP.

world.headline: Estonia to close all border crossings with Russia
world.summary: Estonia will shut its three crossings with Russia from 1 December after foiling what it says was a GRU-ordered plot to blow up and burn the Threod Systems drone factory near Tallinn; eight Latvian residents were detained.
world.context: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the Baltic states have accused Moscow of a hybrid campaign of sabotage across Europe. In August an arson attack hit another Estonian defence firm, Milrem Robotics, which Estonia also blamed on Russia. Prime Minister Kristen Michal links the attacks to Estonia's support for Ukraine.

world.headline: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest over public media
world.summary: Organisers say 350,000 to 400,000 people rallied in Prague's Letná Plain against a plan to scrap licence fees and fund Czech TV and Radio from the state budget, which Reuters says would cut their funding by 15%.
world.context: Andrej Babiš became prime minister in December 2025, leading a coalition of his populist ANO party and two Eurosceptic right-wing parties. In late October parliament pushed the bill through its first reading overnight, triggering weeks of protests and a strike at the public broadcasters. Critics compare it to Hungary under Viktor Orbán; Babiš says no one wants to control public media.

world.headline: Burnham to say UK lost more than it gained from Brexit
world.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will say on Monday that 'the Brexit we were given has not worked', calling it a needlessly hard Brexit, ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit where he wants deals on food, energy and youth mobility.
world.context: The UK voted to leave the EU in 2016 and left in 2020. Keir Starmer struck a first 'reset' deal with the EU in May 2025, and Burnham, who has since replaced him, wants to go further while ruling out a return to the single market, customs union or free movement.

interesting.headline: Anthropic's giant IPO due this week
interesting.summary: Anthropic's stock market listing this week, together with Nvidia's quarterly results on Tuesday, is seen as a test of the AI-driven tech rally, and Asian shares fell ahead of them.
interesting.context: Anthropic is the maker of the Claude AI models and a main rival of OpenAI.

interesting.headline: England end Spain's 43-game unbeaten run
interesting.summary: England beat world champions Spain 3-2 in Madrid, leading 3-0 through Kane, Konsa and White before Anderson's red card let Spain back in. It was Spain's first defeat since March 2024 and sent England top of their Nations League group.

interesting.headline: Vulcan rocket failure destroys 40 Amazon satellites
interesting.summary: ULA's Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes after launch from Florida, losing 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites in the first total mission failure in ULA's 20-year history. It was the first of 38 launches Amazon bought to challenge Starlink.
interesting.context: Vulcan is also contracted to fly about half of the US military's national security launches in the next few years.

interesting.headline: GTA 6 is days from launch
interesting.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI comes out on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S this week after ten years of work, thousands of staff and about a billion dollars, and a leaked 34-song soundtrack lists Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey and SZA.

events.title: UN talks on rules for autonomous 'killer robot' weapons
World Court rules on whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: Zelensky urged the US and Elon Musk to lift speed limits on Starshield terminals, saying Ukrainian interceptor drones lose connection at 161 km/h and cannot catch Russian jet-powered drones. He also said Ukrainian strikes have knocked out 55% of Russia's oil-refining capacity, and a Coalition of the Willing meeting is being prepared to set Europe's stance in peace talks.
ongoing.context: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 after annexing Crimea in 2014. After Ukraine pushed Russian forces back in 2022, the front largely froze into a war of attrition with drone and missile strikes on energy sites. In 2025 the US began pushing both sides toward a peace deal, and talks over territory and security guarantees continue.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude sank after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, unconfirmed independently, as a third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, reached the region.
ongoing.context: Decades of hostility over Iran's nuclear programme turned into open war at the end of February this year, when fighting broke out in the Middle East. Iran then restricted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, which carries about a fifth of the world's oil, and the US answered with a naval blockade of Iranian ports and escorts for tankers.

ongoing.title: Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
ongoing.update: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for an outsider to lead Nvidia and gave its board 10 days to show it complied with export controls on chips to China, while the petition to reinstate Jensen Huang passed 165,000 signatures. Megaspeed says Alice Huang left it in August 2025; Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday.
ongoing.context: In late October The New York Times revealed that Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence suspects of working for China. US officials suspect Singapore-based Megaspeed helped route Nvidia chips to China. Huang resigned as CEO last Thursday and is due to testify to Congress.

ongoing.title: Saudi Arabia-Houthi fighting
ongoing.update: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces withdrew from the Bab al-Mandab Strait area to defend their interim capital Aden, leaving the Houthis in control of the key Red Sea gateway; the Houthis also freed 600 government fighters.
ongoing.context: Yemen's civil war began in 2014 when the Houthis seized Sanaa, and a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015. An informal truce collapsed in July this year when the Houthis declared a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, and in September they seized ground at Bab al-Mandab, pushing up oil prices since Saudi exports relied on the Red Sea while Hormuz was closed.
